A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HELM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HELM training and benchmark results, curvature analysis, and component ablations in Tables 1–4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original HELM experiments and adds translation results, hyperbolic-model comparisons, computational measurements, embedding case studies, and training-checkpoint evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same MICE, HMLA, HOPE, hyperbolic RMSNorm, SwiGLU, and decoder procedures. The additional experiments do not document a revised algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: v2 adds machine translation on IWSLT’14 and WMT’14 in Appendix D.2, substantially extending task coverage beyond the retained multiple-choice benchmarks. Wikipedia training and the original five question-answering benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds a 115M Hypformer comparator on the five question-answering benchmarks (Table 5) and reported translation comparisons against HAT, HNN++, and HyboNet (Table 6). v1’s LLaMA, DeepSeekV3, and internal ablation comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include translation evaluation using BLEU, final-layer embedding-norm comparisons, runtime and peak-memory profiling on four A100 GPUs, and 1B-model evaluations at 4B and 4.5B training tokens. Existing question-answering shot settings and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds semantic-hierarchy case studies (Section 5.3), computational-overhead analysis (Appendix D.1), and checkpoint comparisons examining persistence of the 1B-model advantage (D.5). The existing curvature, HMLA, and positional-encoding ablations remain, with updated HELM result rows.

E5.justification: v1 gives point estimates without run counts. v2 first reports three-run averages with ± uncertainty for the 100M-scale models and ten-run computational measurements with standard deviations omitted. It explicitly acknowledges missing repeated-run uncertainty for 1B models and missing statistics for ablation baselines.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces smaller-model point estimates with three-run summaries: HELM-MICE’s MMLU value changes from 24.7 to 24.4 and its reported average from 24.2 to 24.1. The 1B endpoint scores remain unchanged. New results include hierarchy measurements, runtime/memory, Hypformer comparisons, translation BLEU scores of 26.3 and 26.5 for HELM-D, and earlier checkpoints.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Propositions 4.1–4.5, and derivations and proofs in Appendices A and B are unchanged. Cross-reference wording and typesetting changes do not alter their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit claim of superior semantic-hierarchy modeling relative to the Euclidean architectures. The main architectural contributions, billion-parameter scaling claim, and claimed benchmark advantages otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets embedding norms as evidence of semantic hierarchy and connects that organization to performance. It also suggests checkpoint advantages could persist with larger corpora, and revises the smaller MICE-versus-dense interpretation from superiority to comparable performance with fewer active parameters. The conclusion’s main limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies profiling on four A100 GPUs, roughly 2M tokens per iteration, and reporting the worst runtime and memory across ranks. Translation setup is identified through Chen et al. [5] rather than fully specified locally. Existing implementation details, training settings, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: The 51 references and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. Appendix D.2 adds limited positioning through direct comparisons with earlier hyperbolic models, distinguishing Hypformer’s component completeness from older architectures to motivate the different comparison settings.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.3 and expands Appendix D with computational analysis, prior-model comparisons, and checkpoint analysis. Most existing prose and the overall section order remain, alongside limited wording, cross-reference, acknowledgment, and publication-front-matter edits.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with hierarchy, computational-cost, prior-model comparison, translation, and checkpoint tables (Tables 3–6 and 9). Existing tables gain uncertainty annotations, and v1 Tables 3–4 become v2 Tables 7–8. Figures 1–3 retain their content.

improvement.justification: Three-run small-model summaries, direct hyperbolic baselines, and computational-cost measurements make the empirical claims easier to assess than in v1. Reporting flaws limit the gain: Table 1 gives DeepSeekV3’s 120M average as 22.2 although its task means average 22.94; Table 3 contains a mean outside its stated range; and Section 5.2 asserts statistical significance without specifying a test. The additions nevertheless provide useful comparative evidence.
